content.title: About
content.content: Plain bottled water is clean drinking water that has been filtered and disinfected, packaged in plastic or glass bottles. It contains no additives, flavorings, or sugars, making it a neutral source of hydration.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Most bottled water is sourced from municipal supplies that undergo additional purification.
PET plastic bottles can be recycled many times, but only a small fraction is actually collected for recycling.
Bottled water often undergoes reverse osmosis, UV treatment, or ozonation to remove microbes and contaminants.
In some countries bottled water is considered safer than tap water due to aging or contaminated pipes.
Global bottled water sales increase each year, especially in hot climate regions.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Water is essential for maintaining blood volume, regulating body temperature, and proper organ function.

items.title: Supports metabolism
items.content: Adequate water intake aids digestion and the elimination of metabolic waste.

items.title: Improves cognitive function
items.content: Even mild dehydration can impair concentration and memory; regular drinking helps keep the mind sharp.

items.title: Reduces kidney stone risk
items.content: Higher water consumption dilutes urine, decreasing the chance of crystal formation.

items.title: Skin health
items.content: Proper hydration supports skin elasticity and overall appearance.

items.title: Plastic micro‑particles
items.content: Long‑term storage in plastic bottles can lead to the release of microscopic plastic particles that may be ingested.

items.title: Environmental impact
items.content: Production and disposal of bottles generate significant CO₂ emissions and waste.

items.title: Lack of minerals
items.content: Unlike mineral water, plain bottled water contains virtually no electrolytes, which may require supplementation from other sources.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Sip water regularly throughout the day, especially before, during, and after physical activity. Keep bottles in a cool place and avoid direct sunlight.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bottles in a dry, cool environment away from direct sunlight. Once opened, consume within 1–2 days and keep the cap tightly sealed.
